merge.book: VYBEON Clean: 250 DIY Household Cleaning Recipes (1.0.0, build 2026.11.16-1)

left_out.reason: DIY hand sanitizer: the FDA advises consumers not to make their own, and a mismeasured batch won't kill germs. Buy a 60 to 95% alcohol sanitizer instead.

relabeled.reason: Relabeled from Disinfect to Sanitize: a hot dryer cycle reduces germs, like recipes 113 and 114, but it is not a verified disinfecting method.

recipes.name: Stone-Safe Soapy Counter Spray
recipes.prepare: Pour the water into a 16-oz spray bottle, add the soap, cap, and tip gently to mix (shaking makes foam).
recipes.apply: Spray the counter, wipe with a damp microfiber cloth, then buff dry with a second cloth. Safe daily cleaner for sealed granite, quartz, marble and laminate.
limits: Dish soap only; no acid, so it will not etch stone. Re-seal stone counters per the installer's schedule.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Make with distilled or boiled-and-cooled water. Label the bottle. Use within 2 weeks; discard sooner if cloudy or smelly.

recipes.name: Vinegar Counter and Backsplash Spray
recipes.prepare: Combine in a labeled 16-oz spray bottle.
recipes.apply: Spray laminate, ceramic tile, glass or stainless counters; wipe with a damp cloth. Cuts light grease and hard-water film.
limits: Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Label the bottle (contents + date). Store capped at room temperature, out of reach of children and pets. Vinegar-and-water mixes keep about 3 months.

recipes.name: Lemon-Peel Infused Vinegar Cleaner
recipes.prepare: Pack the peels in a clean glass jar and cover with the vinegar. Cap and steep 1-2 weeks in a cool, dark cupboard. Strain out the peels, then mix 1 part infused vinegar with 1 part water in a spray bottle.
recipes.apply: Use like plain vinegar spray on tile, sinks and stainless; the citrus mainly softens the vinegar smell.
limits: Discard the infusion if mold appears on peels during steeping.

Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Label the bottle (contents + date). Store capped at room temperature, out of reach of children and pets. Vinegar-and-water mixes keep about 3 months.

recipes.name: Range Hood and Stovetop Degreaser
recipes.prepare: Wearing gloves, dissolve the washing soda in the hot water in a heat-safe measuring cup, stir in the soap, and let cool to warm before pouring into a spray bottle.
recipes.apply: With the stove off and cool, spray greasy enamel or stainless surfaces, wait 2 minutes, wipe with a damp sponge, then rinse-wipe with clean water and dry.
limits: Washing soda is strongly alkaline: wear gloves and eye protection. Do not use on aluminum, waxed or oiled wood, wool, silk, or true linoleum; it can dull paint.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Make with distilled or boiled-and-cooled water. Label the bottle. Use within 2 weeks; discard sooner if cloudy or smelly.

recipes.name: Baking Soda Stovetop Paste
recipes.prepare: Stir together in a small bowl to a toothpaste-like paste.
recipes.apply: On a cool stovetop, rub paste onto cooked-on spots with a damp non-scratch sponge in small circles. Wipe away with a damp cloth and dry.
limits: Check glass-ceramic cooktop instructions first; some makers specify their own cream.
Mild abrasive: can scratch high-gloss finishes, acrylic tubs, polished stone and soft plastics. Use a soft cloth, light pressure, and test first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Overnight Oven Interior Paste
ing: 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar (for the rinse step, kept in a separate spray bottle)
recipes.prepare: Mix baking soda and water into a spreadable paste. Put vinegar in its own spray bottle.
recipes.apply: Remove racks. Spread paste over the cool oven interior, avoiding heating elements, gas ports and the door gasket. Leave 12 hours. Wipe off with a damp cloth and plastic scraper, then mist leftover white residue with vinegar so it foams, and wipe clean with water.
limits: Do not use on self-clean or steam-clean oven linings unless the manual permits; never run a self-clean cycle with paste inside.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Microwave Lemon Steam
recipes.prepare: Squeeze both lemon halves into a microwave-safe bowl of water and drop in the halves.
recipes.apply: Microwave on high 3 minutes, then leave the door closed 5 minutes so steam loosens splatters. Remove the bowl with mitts, wipe the interior and turntable with a damp cloth.
limits: Water can superheat: place a wooden spoon or microwave-safe stir stick in the bowl.
Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Range Hood Filter Soak
recipes.prepare: Fill a sink or tub with the hot water and stir in baking soda and dish soap until dissolved.
recipes.apply: Remove the metal mesh filter, submerge 15 minutes, scrub gently with a soft brush, rinse with hot water and air-dry completely before reinstalling.
limits: Baking soda may darken bare aluminum filters; check the hood manual. Never use on charcoal (recirculating) filters, which are replaced, not washed.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Stainless Appliance Wipe and Buff
ing: 1/2 teaspoon food-grade mineral oil (for buffing step)
recipes.prepare: Mix water and soap in a bowl. Keep the mineral oil separate.
recipes.apply: Wipe the appliance with a cloth dampened in the soapy water, following the grain. Rinse-wipe and dry. Put a few drops of mineral oil on a dry cloth and buff with the grain to reduce fingerprints.
limits: Skip the oil on handles you want non-slip. Not for black-stainless or coated finishes unless the maker permits.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Salt and Lemon Cutting Board Scrub
recipes.prepare: Sprinkle salt over the dampened wood or plastic board.
recipes.apply: Scrub with the cut side of the lemon, squeezing as you go. Let sit 5 minutes, scrape off, then wash with hot soapy water, rinse and stand upright to dry. Oil wood boards with food-grade mineral oil when dry.
limits: Removes stains and odors only; after raw meat, poultry or seafood, follow recipe #021 (Cutting Board Sanitizing Flood (USDA Method)) to sanitize.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Coffee Maker Descaling Cycle
ing: Equal parts white distilled vinegar and water to fill the reservoir (for a 10-cup maker: 5 cups vinegar + 5 cups water)
plain water for two rinse cycles
recipes.prepare: Fill the reservoir with the vinegar-water mix. Insert an empty paper filter.
recipes.apply: Brew half the reservoir, switch off and let sit 30 minutes, then finish brewing. Discard. Run two full cycles of plain water to remove taste. Wash carafe and basket in hot soapy water.
limits: Follow your machine's manual first; some makers (e.g., pod machines) specify their own descaler.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Lemon Kettle Descaler
ing: water to fill the kettle halfway
recipes.prepare: Pour lemon juice into the kettle and add water to the half-full mark.
recipes.apply: Bring to a boil, switch off and let stand 1 hour. Pour out, scrub any remaining scale with a soft brush, rinse twice and boil one kettle of fresh water to discard.
limits: Not for kettles with exposed heating coils unless the manual allows.
Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Dishwasher Refresh (Two-Step)
recipes.prepare: Remove and rinse the filter. Pour vinegar into an upright dishwasher-safe cup.
recipes.apply: Step 1: set the cup on the top rack of an empty dishwasher and run the hottest cycle. Step 2: sprinkle baking soda across the bottom and run a short hot cycle. Wipe door edges with a damp cloth.
limits: Check the manual; some makers advise against frequent vinegar use on rubber seals. Limit to once a month.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Garbage Disposal Foam Clean
recipes.prepare: Have all ingredients measured before starting.
recipes.apply: With the disposal off, pour baking soda into the drain, then the vinegar. Let it foam 10 minutes, then flush with hot water while running the disposal for 15 seconds.
limits: Never use within 24 hours of a commercial drain opener or bleach; flush with plenty of water first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Ice and Salt Disposal Scour
recipes.prepare: Measure ingredients into a bowl.
recipes.apply: With cold water running, drop ice and salt into the disposal and run it until grinding stops (about 30 seconds). The ice knocks residue off the grinding chamber.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
Salt left on metal promotes rust: rinse and dry metal thoroughly.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Refrigerator Interior Wipe
recipes.prepare: Dissolve baking soda in the warm water in a bowl.
recipes.apply: Remove food and shelves. Wipe walls, shelves and drawers with a cloth dipped in the solution, rinse-wipe with plain water and dry. Wash removable glass shelves only after they reach room temperature to prevent cracking.
limits: For spills from raw meat juices, sanitize afterward with recipe #022 (Food-Contact Counter Sanitizer (Quart Batch)).
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Stainless Steel Sink Scrub
recipes.prepare: Stir into a soft paste.
recipes.apply: Rub onto the wet sink with a non-scratch sponge, following the grain. Rinse well and dry with a towel to prevent water spots.
limits: Mild abrasive: can scratch high-gloss finishes, acrylic tubs, polished stone and soft plastics. Use a soft cloth, light pressure, and test first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Burnt Pot Simmer Soak
ing: 2 cups water (or enough to cover the burnt area)
recipes.prepare: Add water and baking soda to the burnt stainless or enameled pot.
recipes.apply: Bring to a gentle simmer 10 minutes, switch off and cool to warm. Scrape loosened food with a wooden spatula and wash with soapy water.
limits: Not for aluminum (darkens), nonstick, or cast iron.
Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Cast Iron Salt Scour
recipes.prepare: Warm the pan slightly on low heat and remove from the burner.
recipes.apply: Add salt and oil and scrub with a folded paper towel held in tongs. Dump salt, rinse quickly with hot water, dry on low heat, then rub a thin film of oil over the surface.
limits: Never soak cast iron or use vinegar or citrus on it; acid strips seasoning.
Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
Salt left on metal promotes rust: rinse and dry metal thoroughly.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Copper Cookware Exterior Polish
recipes.prepare: Mix into a smooth paste.
recipes.apply: Rub onto tarnished unlacquered copper exteriors with a soft cloth, let sit 5 minutes, rinse with warm water and dry immediately.
limits: Not for lacquered copper, copper-look plated items, or tin-lined interiors. Acid paste: keep off nearby stone counters.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
Salt left on metal promotes rust: rinse and dry metal thoroughly.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Cutting Board Sanitizing Flood (USDA Method)
ing: 1 tablespoon regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else.
recipes.apply: First wash the board with hot soapy water and rinse. Flood the surface with the solution and let it stand several minutes (at least 1 minute, visibly wet). Rinse with clean water, then air-dry or pat dry with clean paper towels.
limits: Use on plastic and solid wood boards that are free of deep cracks; replace boards with deep grooves.

Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Food-Contact Counter Sanitizer (Quart Batch)
ing: 1 teaspoon regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else. Use a dedicated spray bottle labeled 'BLEACH SANITIZER - DO NOT MIX'.
recipes.apply: After cleaning with hot soapy water and rinsing, spray the counter until evenly wet. Leave at least 1 minute, then rinse with clean water and let air-dry. Use after preparing raw meat, poultry, seafood or eggs.
limits: Not for natural stone, wood counters, or unsealed surfaces; use an EPA-registered food-contact sanitizer that lists your surface instead.

Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Sponge, Dishcloth and Potholder Soak
ing: 3/4 cup regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else.
recipes.apply: Rinse food out of sponges and cloths. Submerge in the solution 5 minutes, rinse thoroughly, and allow to air-dry before use. Alternatively, wash cloths and potholders in the hot cycle and dry on high.
limits: Bleach will spot colored cloths. Replace worn or smelly sponges often.

Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Kitchen Sink and Drain Sanitize (Weekly)
ing: 1 tablespoon regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe) (sink)
1 tablespoon bleach + 1 quart water (drain, separate batch)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else. Make the sink batch and the drain batch in separate labeled containers.
recipes.apply: Clean the sink with soap and rinse. Wipe basin, faucet and handles with the gallon solution and let air-dry. Pour the quart batch slowly into the drain and disposal. Wash the sink strainer weekly.
limits: Do not use within 24 hours of vinegar, baking soda-vinegar foams, or drain products; run water for 1 minute first.

Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Kitchen High-Touch Disinfecting Wipe-Down
ing: 4 teaspoons regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else.
recipes.apply: When someone in the home is sick: clean refrigerator handles, faucet handles, cabinet pulls and switch plates with soapy water, then wipe with the solution so surfaces stay visibly wet at least 1 minute. Rinse food-contact areas with water and let air-dry.
limits: Apply with a cloth on switch plates; never spray electrical fixtures.

Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
Electrical: switch off and unplug first. Spray the cloth, never the device. Follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which override this recipe.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought kitchen spray cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Warm Vinegar Soap-Scum Spray
recipes.prepare: Warm the vinegar in the microwave 30-45 seconds (warm, not boiling). Pour into a spray bottle, add soap, and tip gently to mix.
recipes.apply: Spray ceramic tile, glass doors or fiberglass tubs, wait 10 minutes, scrub with a non-scratch sponge, and rinse thoroughly with water.
limits: Never use on stone showers or near a toilet that has a bleach tablet in the tank.

Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Label the bottle (contents + date). Store capped at room temperature, out of reach of children and pets. Use within 1 month.

recipes.name: Tub and Sink Soft Scrub
recipes.prepare: Stir together into a creamy paste.
recipes.apply: Apply to a damp tub or sink with a sponge, scrub in circles, rinse well. Good on porcelain, enamel and fiberglass rings.
limits: Use very light pressure on acrylic tubs.
Mild abrasive: can scratch high-gloss finishes, acrylic tubs, polished stone and soft plastics. Use a soft cloth, light pressure, and test first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Basic Grout Paste (Sealed Ceramic Tile)
recipes.prepare: Mix into a thick paste.
recipes.apply: Work into grout lines with an old toothbrush, wait 5 minutes, scrub, then rinse with a wet sponge and dry.
limits: Mild abrasive: can scratch high-gloss finishes, acrylic tubs, polished stone and soft plastics. Use a soft cloth, light pressure, and test first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Peroxide Grout-Brightening Paste
recipes.prepare: Mix fresh in a small dish right before use.
recipes.apply: Apply to stained light-colored grout, leave 10 minutes, scrub with a toothbrush, and rinse thoroughly with water.
limits: May lighten colored grout; test a hidden line.

3% hydrogen peroxide can lighten fabrics, carpet, wood and hair. Never mix with vinegar in the same bottle (forms corrosive peracetic acid) and never with bleach. Keep it in its original brown bottle; light breaks it down.
Mild abrasive: can scratch high-gloss finishes, acrylic tubs, polished stone and soft plastics. Use a soft cloth, light pressure, and test first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Keep 3% hydrogen peroxide in its original brown bottle; mix only the amount you need. Discard mixed paste after use.

recipes.name: Toilet Bowl Baking Soda Fizz
recipes.prepare: Remove any in-tank or clip-on bowl cleaner and flush twice first so no bleach or toilet-cleaner residue remains.
recipes.apply: Sprinkle baking soda around the bowl, pour vinegar over it, let it fizz 10 minutes, scrub with the toilet brush and flush.
limits: NEVER use if bleach, a bleach tablet, or a commercial toilet-bowl cleaner is in the bowl or tank: acids plus bleach release toxic chlorine gas.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Overnight Hard-Water Ring Soak
recipes.prepare: Turn off the toilet supply valve and flush to lower the water below the ring. Confirm no bleach products are in the tank or bowl.
recipes.apply: Pour vinegar over the ring so it is covered; stuff paper towels against the ring and soak them in vinegar if needed. Leave overnight, scrub with a pumice stone made for toilets (wet), turn water back on and flush.
limits: Never combine with bleach or toilet-bowl cleaners.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Faucet Hard-Water Wrap
recipes.prepare: Soak the paper towels in vinegar.
recipes.apply: Wrap the towels around chrome faucet bases and spouts with mineral crust, leave 30 minutes, remove, scrub with a soft toothbrush, rinse and buff dry.
limits: Not for brass, gold, oil-rubbed bronze, matte black or 'living' finishes; keep off stone vanities.

Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Showerhead Bag Soak
recipes.prepare: Pour vinegar into the bag.
recipes.apply: Slip the bag over a chrome showerhead so the nozzles are submerged, secure with the rubber band, and leave 1 hour. Remove, run hot water 1 minute and scrub nozzles with an old toothbrush.
limits: Not for brass, nickel or specialty finishes; check the maker's guidance.

Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Shower Door Track Foam
recipes.prepare: Vacuum loose debris from the track first.
recipes.apply: Sprinkle baking soda into the track, drizzle vinegar over it, let foam 5 minutes, scrub with an old toothbrush, then wipe out with a damp cloth.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Daily After-Shower Mist
recipes.prepare: Combine in a labeled spray bottle.
recipes.apply: After showering, lightly mist walls and glass, then squeegee. Helps prevent soap-scum and water-spot build-up.
limits: Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Label the bottle (contents + date). Store capped at room temperature, out of reach of children and pets. Vinegar-and-water mixes keep about 3 months.

recipes.name: Shower Curtain Liner Machine Wash
recipes.prepare: Add detergent and baking soda to the drum with the liner and towels (towels scrub as they tumble). Put vinegar in the fabric-softener dispenser.
recipes.apply: Wash on warm, gentle cycle. Hang the liner back up immediately to drip-dry; do not machine-dry plastic.
limits: Do not add chlorine bleach to a load that uses vinegar.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
Fabric: check the care label and test on an inside seam or hidden area for colorfastness before treating.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Bath Mat and Tub Mat Scrub
recipes.prepare: Mix baking soda and soap into a paste.
recipes.apply: Lay the rubber or vinyl mat in the tub, scrub both sides (especially suction cups) with a brush, rinse well and hang to dry.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Cultured-Marble and Solid-Surface Vanity Wipe
recipes.prepare: Mix in a bowl or spray bottle.
recipes.apply: Wipe with a soft cloth, rinse-wipe and dry. Gentle, non-abrasive and non-acidic for cultured marble, solid surface and natural stone vanities.
limits: No scouring pads or powders on cultured marble gel-coat.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Make with distilled or boiled-and-cooled water. Label the bottle. Use within 2 weeks; discard sooner if cloudy or smelly.

recipes.name: Chrome Fixture Shine
recipes.prepare: Combine in a small spray bottle.
recipes.apply: Mist a microfiber cloth (not the fixture), wipe chrome faucets and towel bars, and buff dry to remove water spots and fingerprints.
limits: Rubbing alcohol is flammable: no flames, sparks or hot surfaces; ventilate. Can damage shellac, lacquer, some paints, acrylic and anti-glare screen coatings.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Label the bottle. Store tightly capped away from heat, flames and sunlight, out of reach of children. Use within 3 months.

recipes.name: Exhaust Fan Grille Soak
recipes.prepare: Switch off the fan at the switch (or breaker) and remove the grille.
recipes.apply: Soak the grille 10 minutes in the soapy water, brush, rinse and dry fully. Vacuum dust from the housing with a brush attachment. Reinstall only when dry.
limits: Electrical: switch off and unplug first. Spray the cloth, never the device. Follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which override this recipe.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought bathroom cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Peroxide Mildew-Stain Spray for Caulk
recipes.prepare: Fit the original brown peroxide bottle with a spray nozzle, or use an opaque spray bottle.
recipes.apply: Spray stained caulk and grout, leave 10 minutes, scrub with a toothbrush, rinse and dry. Fix the moisture source and ventilate; replace caulk that stays stained.
limits: For large mold areas (more than about 10 square feet), follow EPA mold guidance.

recipes.apply: Wash, rinse and dry. Dab small rust spots with vinegar on a rag, wait 10 minutes, scrub with a wire brush, rinse, dry fully and touch up with rust-inhibiting paint.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Outdoor Cushion Scrub
recipes.prepare: Check the tag: remove machine-washable covers and launder them instead.
recipes.apply: Brush loose dirt off. Scrub with the soapy water and a soft brush, rinse thoroughly with a hose until no suds remain, and stand on edge in the sun to dry.
limits: Fabric: check the care label and test on an inside seam or hidden area for colorfastness before treating.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Grill Grate Baking Soda Paste
recipes.prepare: Let the grill cool completely. Mix into a paste.
recipes.apply: Coat grates with paste, leave 30 minutes, scrub with a grill brush, rinse and dry. Heat the grill 10 minutes to burn off residue before cooking.
limits: Inspect wire brushes for loose bristles; bristles left on grates can be swallowed.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Garage Floor Oil Stain Two-Step
recipes.prepare: Step 1: cover the fresh oil spot with litter, grind in with your shoe, leave 24 hours, then sweep up and bag.
recipes.apply: Step 2: wearing gloves and eye protection, dissolve washing soda in hot water, scrub the stain with a stiff brush, and rinse with a hose toward lawn or gravel (not a storm drain).
limits: Dispose of oily litter as household trash, or per your local hazardous-waste rules.
Washing soda is strongly alkaline: wear gloves and eye protection. Do not use on aluminum, waxed or oiled wood, wool, silk, or true linoleum; it can dull paint.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Concrete Rust-Stain Lemon Treatment
recipes.prepare: Test on a hidden area: acid can etch or lighten concrete.
recipes.apply: Pour lemon juice over the rust stain on plain, unsealed concrete, leave 10 minutes, scrub with a stiff brush and rinse well.
limits: Not for sealed, stained, colored or stamped concrete, pavers, or stone.

Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Car Body Hand Wash
ing: second bucket of clean rinse water
recipes.prepare: Park in the shade with a cool body panel.
recipes.apply: Wash top-down with a microfiber mitt, rinsing the mitt in the clean bucket between panels. Rinse and dry with microfiber towels.
limits: Dish soap removes wax and sealant; re-wax afterward or use a car-wash soap for routine washes.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Wheel and Brake-Dust Scrub
recipes.prepare: Let wheels cool. Mix the solution.
recipes.apply: Scrub painted or clear-coated wheels with a soft wheel brush, rinse thoroughly, and dry.
limits: Not for polished, uncoated aluminum or chrome-plated wheels unless the maker permits.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Garden Tool Wash and Oil
ing: 1 teaspoon light machine oil or vegetable oil
recipes.prepare: Knock off dried soil.
recipes.apply: Scrub tools in the soapy water, rinse, and dry completely. Wipe metal parts with a thin coat of oil to prevent rust.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Rusty Tool Vinegar Soak
ing: White distilled vinegar to cover the tool (about 4 cups)
1 tablespoon baking soda in 1 quart water (neutralizing rinse)
recipes.prepare: Place the rusty tool in a plastic tub and cover with vinegar.
recipes.apply: Soak 12-24 hours, scrub with a wire brush, dip in the baking-soda rinse to stop the acid, rinse with water, dry immediately and oil.
limits: Long soaks can etch metal; check every few hours. Not for tools with wooden handles submerged.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Outdoor Trash Can Wash and Deodorize
recipes.prepare: Empty the can on a lawn or gravel area.
recipes.apply: Scrub the inside with a long-handled brush and soapy water, rinse, tip upside down to dry in the sun, then sprinkle baking soda into the bottom.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Vinyl Siding Mildew-Stain Wash
recipes.prepare: Wearing gloves and eye protection, dissolve the powder. Wet nearby plants with plain water first.
recipes.apply: Working bottom to top in shade, scrub siding with a soft long-handled brush, then rinse top to bottom with a hose. Rinse plants again.
limits: Oxygen bleach (sodium percarbonate): wear gloves; not for wool, silk, leather or metallic trims. Do not combine with chlorine bleach or vinegar. Follow the product label.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Wood Deck Oxygen Cleaner
recipes.prepare: Sweep the deck. Dissolve the powder (gloves and eye protection). Wet plants.
recipes.apply: Apply with a pump sprayer or mop, keep wet 10-15 minutes, scrub with a deck brush, and rinse thoroughly. Let dry 48 hours before sealing.
limits: May lighten wood; test first. Not for composite decking unless the maker permits.
Oxygen bleach (sodium percarbonate): wear gloves; not for wool, silk, leather or metallic trims. Do not combine with chlorine bleach or vinegar. Follow the product label.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Bird Feeder Hot-Soap Clean
recipes.prepare: Empty old seed into the trash.
recipes.apply: Disassemble and scrub with a bottle brush, rinse very thoroughly, and dry completely in the sun before refilling. Clean every two weeks, more often in wet weather.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Hummingbird Feeder Rinse
ing: 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar (for mold spots)
recipes.prepare: Discard old nectar.
recipes.apply: Rinse with hot water and scrub ports with a small brush. If black mold spots appear, soak parts in the vinegar plus 1 cup of the hot water for 1 hour, scrub, then rinse thoroughly with plain water before refilling. Do not use soap, which can leave residue.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Workbench Grease Cut
recipes.prepare: Dissolve washing soda (gloves).
recipes.apply: Scrub sealed or painted workbench surfaces, rinse-wipe with plain water and dry.
limits: Washing soda is strongly alkaline: wear gloves and eye protection. Do not use on aluminum, waxed or oiled wood, wool, silk, or true linoleum; it can dull paint.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Outdoor Light Fixture Wash
recipes.prepare: Turn off the circuit and let bulbs cool.
recipes.apply: Remove the glass, empty insects, wash, rinse and dry completely before reassembling.
limits: Electrical: switch off and unplug first. Spray the cloth, never the device. Follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which override this recipe.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Patio Umbrella and Awning Mildew Wash
recipes.prepare: Open the umbrella on a dry day.
recipes.apply: Brush off dirt, scrub stained areas with a soft brush, rinse well, and leave open in the sun until fully dry.
limits: Check fabric maker instructions; some acrylic fabrics specify their own cleaners.
Fabric: check the care label and test on an inside seam or hidden area for colorfastness before treating.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Kids' Outdoor Plastic Toy Scrub
recipes.prepare: Mix in a bucket.
recipes.apply: Scrub slides, sand toys and ride-ons, rinse with a hose and dry in the sun.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Terra-Cotta Pot Mineral Crust Soak
recipes.prepare: Empty and brush out soil.
recipes.apply: Soak pots 30 minutes, scrub white crust with a stiff brush, then soak in plain water 15 minutes and rinse well before planting.
limits: Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Mop Bucket and Mop Head Refresh
recipes.prepare: Rinse the mop head and bucket.
recipes.apply: Soak the mop head 30 minutes, rinse well, wring, and hang to dry fully in fresh air. Scrub the bucket with the leftover solution, rinse and dry upside down.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Outdoor Trash Can Disinfecting
ing: 5 tablespoons (1/3 cup) regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else.
recipes.apply: After washing, wet the can's inside with the solution and keep it wet at least 1 minute. Pour the used solution into a household sink or toilet (sanitary sewer), not onto plants, soil or a storm drain. Rinse and dry upside down.
limits: Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Reused Plastic Plant Pot Disinfecting
ing: 5 tablespoons (1/3 cup) regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else.
recipes.apply: Scrub off all soil and wash. Submerge plastic pots or wipe so they stay wet at least 1 minute, then rinse thoroughly with water and dry before planting.
limits: Not for terra cotta, which absorbs bleach; use the mineral-crust soak and sun-dry instead.

Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Outdoor Play Equipment Disinfecting (After Illness)
ing: 5 tablespoons (1/3 cup) regular, unscented liquid chlorine bleach labeled 5%-9% sodium hypochlorite (not splashless, scented, or color-safe)
recipes.prepare: Put on gloves and eye protection and open a window or run a fan. Pour the water into a clean, labeled bucket or bottle first, then add the bleach. Add nothing else.
recipes.apply: Wash hard plastic toys or play-set handles with soapy water, then wipe with the solution so surfaces stay wet at least 1 minute. Rinse thoroughly with water (children put hands and toys in mouths) and dry before use.
limits: Not for wood play sets or fabric parts.

Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought outdoor or utility cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Silver Tarnish Foil Bath
recipes.prepare: Line a glass or plastic basin with foil, shiny side up. Add baking soda and salt, then pour in the hot water and stir.
recipes.apply: Lay sterling or silver-plated pieces on the foil so they touch it, fully submerged, for 2-5 minutes. Remove with tongs, rinse, and buff dry with a soft cloth.
limits: Removes decorative dark patina in engraved designs; not for antiques of value, pieces with pearls, stones, glued parts or hollow handles.
Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
Salt left on metal promotes rust: rinse and dry metal thoroughly.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought specialty cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Unlacquered Brass Lemon-Soda Polish
recipes.prepare: Mix in a small bowl (it will foam); wait until foaming stops.
recipes.apply: Rub onto unlacquered brass with a soft cloth, leave 5 minutes, rinse with warm water and dry completely.
limits: Not for lacquered or brass-plated items (test with a magnet: plated steel attracts it). Keep acid off stone.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix just before use; paste dries out and loses fizz. Discard leftovers in the trash or drain.

recipes.name: Solid Gold Jewelry Soak
recipes.prepare: Mix in a small bowl.
recipes.apply: Soak solid gold and diamond pieces 15 minutes, brush gently with a soft baby toothbrush, rinse over a closed drain or in a strainer, and dry with a lint-free cloth.
limits: Not for pearls, opals, emeralds, turquoise, coral or glued settings.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Pearl Gentle Wipe
recipes.prepare: Dampen the cloth slightly.
recipes.apply: Wipe each pearl after wearing, then lay flat on a dry towel to dry before storing. Never soak strung pearls; wet silk stretches.
limits: No vinegar, lemon, alcohol, or ultrasonic cleaners on pearls.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Costume Jewelry Spot Clean
recipes.prepare: Mix in a cup.
recipes.apply: Dip a swab, squeeze nearly dry, and wipe the metal and stones. Wipe with a plain-water swab and dry immediately; never submerge glued pieces.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Computer Keyboard Clean
ing: 1 teaspoon 70% isopropyl alcohol (if the maker permits)
recipes.prepare: Shut down and unplug the computer or remove keyboard batteries. Turn the keyboard over and tap out crumbs.
recipes.apply: Lightly dampen a cloth or swab with alcohol (never dripping) and wipe keycaps and between keys. Let dry 5 minutes before reconnecting.
limits: Rubbing alcohol is flammable: no flames, sparks or hot surfaces; ventilate. Can damage shellac, lacquer, some paints, acrylic and anti-glare screen coatings.
Electrical: switch off and unplug first. Spray the cloth, never the device. Follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which override this recipe.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Label the bottle. Store tightly capped away from heat, flames and sunlight, out of reach of children. Use within 3 months.

recipes.name: TV Remote Swab Clean
recipes.prepare: Remove the batteries.
recipes.apply: Wipe buttons and casing with a lightly dampened swab; use the toothpick to lift grime from seams. Dry, then reinstall batteries.
limits: Rubbing alcohol is flammable: no flames, sparks or hot surfaces; ventilate. Can damage shellac, lacquer, some paints, acrylic and anti-glare screen coatings.
Electrical: switch off and unplug first. Spray the cloth, never the device. Follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which override this recipe.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Label the bottle. Store tightly capped away from heat, flames and sunlight, out of reach of children. Use within 3 months.

recipes.name: Piano Key Wipe
recipes.prepare: Mix in a cup.
recipes.apply: Dip one cloth, wring until barely damp, and wipe keys front to back one at a time (never side to side, which pushes moisture between keys). Dry each key with the second cloth.
limits: Ivory keys: plain water only. No alcohol or vinegar.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Vinyl and Faux-Wood Blind Clean
recipes.prepare: Mix in a bowl.
recipes.apply: Close the blinds. Wear the sock on your hand, dip, wring, and run each slat between your fingers. Reverse the slats and repeat. Let air-dry.
limits: Real wood blinds: dust only or use a barely damp soapy cloth. Metal blinds: use soapy water to avoid corrosion.

Acidic (vinegar or citrus): do not use on marble, limestone, travertine, onyx, granite or other natural stone, concrete counters, unsealed grout, waxed or oiled wood, or cast iron. Test a hidden spot first.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Houseplant Leaf Dusting
recipes.prepare: Support each leaf from below with one hand.
recipes.apply: Wipe broad leaves with a cloth dampened in plain water. For many small leaves, rinse the plant in a lukewarm shower. Do not use leaf-shine oils or milk.
limits: Fuzzy-leaved plants (like African violets): soft dry brush only.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: High Chair Tray and Seat Clean
recipes.prepare: Remove the tray and any removable straps (check the manual).
recipes.apply: Wash the tray in the sink or dishwasher (if labeled safe). Wipe the seat and frame with the soapy water, rinse-wipe and dry. Sanitize the tray afterward if desired with the high chair tray sanitizer below.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Infant Feeding Item Hand-Wash (CDC Steps)
ing: 1 clean basin used only for infant feeding items
recipes.prepare: Wash hands with soap and water for 20 seconds. Take bottles fully apart (nipples, rings, valves, caps).
recipes.apply: Rinse parts under running water. Fill the basin with hot soapy water, scrub each part with the brush, and squeeze water through nipple holes. Rinse under running water, then air-dry on a clean, unused towel in a dust-free area. Do not rub dry with a dish towel.
limits: Do not wash directly in the sink. Sanitize daily if the baby is under 2 months, premature or has a weakened immune system (see recipes below).
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Hard Plastic Toy Wash
recipes.prepare: Remove batteries from battery-operated toys (surface clean those only).
recipes.apply: Wash, scrub with a brush, rinse and air-dry. Many hard plastic toys can go on the dishwasher top rack.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought specialty cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Candle Jar Wax Removal
ing: Boiling water to fill the jar
recipes.prepare: Scrape out as much wax as possible. Set the jar on a towel in the sink.
recipes.apply: Pour in boiling water; wax melts and floats. Let cool until wax hardens on top, lift it out, then wash the jar with dish soap.
limits: Thin or cracked glass can break; let the jar reach room temperature first.
Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Hairbrush and Comb Soak
recipes.prepare: Pull hair out of the brush with a comb or your fingers.
recipes.apply: Soak plastic combs and brush heads 15 minutes (bristles down for brushes with cushions), scrub with an old toothbrush, rinse and dry bristles-down.
limits: Wooden or boar-bristle brushes: dip bristles only, do not soak.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Makeup Brush Wash
recipes.prepare: Mix in a small bowl.
recipes.apply: Swirl brush tips in the water, massage gently on your palm, rinse until clear, squeeze out water, reshape, and dry lying flat or tips-down so water does not loosen the glue.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Reusable Water Bottle Soak
ing: warm water to fill the bottle
recipes.prepare: Disassemble lids, straws and seals.
recipes.apply: Fill with warm water and baking soda, cap and shake, then soak overnight. Scrub with a bottle brush, wash parts in soapy water, rinse and air-dry open.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Yoga and Exercise Mat Spray
recipes.prepare: Combine in a spray bottle.
recipes.apply: Mist the mat, wipe with a cloth, rinse-wipe with plain water and hang to air-dry out of direct sun.
limits: Natural rubber mats: avoid vinegar and oils; follow the maker's care guide.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Make with distilled or boiled-and-cooled water. Label the bottle. Use within 2 weeks; discard sooner if cloudy or smelly.

recipes.name: Sneaker Sole and Upper Scrub
recipes.prepare: Remove laces and insoles. Bang out loose dirt.
recipes.apply: Scrub soles and canvas or synthetic uppers with a toothbrush dipped in the solution, wipe with a damp cloth, stuff with paper towels and air-dry away from heat.
limits: Not for suede or leather uppers.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
Fabric: check the care label and test on an inside seam or hidden area for colorfastness before treating.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Cool-Mist Humidifier Descale
recipes.prepare: Unplug and empty the humidifier. Check the manual for approved cleaners.
recipes.apply: Pour the vinegar-water mix into the tank and base, soak 30 minutes, scrub scale with a soft brush, then rinse at least three times with plain water until no vinegar smell remains. Air-dry. Refill with distilled water.
limits: Electrical: switch off and unplug first. Spray the cloth, never the device. Follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which override this recipe.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.name: Washable Vacuum Filter Rinse
recipes.prepare: Unplug the vacuum. Confirm the filter is marked washable.
recipes.apply: Tap out dust outdoors, rinse the filter under lukewarm water until it runs clear (no soap unless the manual says so), shake, and air-dry 24 hours before reinstalling.
limits: Never reinstall a damp filter; it can damage the motor.
Electrical: switch off and unplug first. Spray the cloth, never the device. Follow the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which override this recipe.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Infant Feeding Items: Boil to Sanitize
recipes.prepare: Wash items first (see hand-wash recipe). Check that the maker says items are safe to boil.
recipes.apply: Place disassembled items in the pot, cover with water, bring to a boil and boil 5 minutes. Remove with clean tongs and air-dry on a clean, unused towel. A dishwasher with hot water and heated drying (or sanitize setting) also sanitizes, without a separate step.
limits: Hot liquid or steam: risk of burns. Use oven mitts and let things cool before handling.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Infant Feeding Items: Bleach Sanitize (When You Cannot Boil)
recipes.prepare: Wash hands. In a clean basin used only for feeding items, add the bleach to the water. Use this only if boiling, steaming or a dishwasher are not available.
recipes.apply: Fully submerge washed items with no air bubbles, squeeze solution through nipple holes, and soak at least 2 minutes. Remove with clean hands or tongs. Do not rinse (rinsing can re-contaminate); air-dry completely before storing.
limits: Chlorine bleach: NEVER mix with vinegar, lemon or other acids, ammonia, rubbing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other cleaner. Ventilate, wear gloves and eye protection. Removes color from fabrics and carpet; corrodes metal if left on. Not for natural stone, wood furniture or floors, or other porous surfaces unless the recipe specifically allows it.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh daily in a labeled, clean container (never a food or drink bottle). Diluted bleach weakens within 24 hours; discard leftovers down a household drain with plenty of water. Keep the bleach jug capped, cool, and locked away from children and pets.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought specialty cleaner (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Mouthed Hard Plastic Toy Sanitize

recipes.name: Trash Can Bottom Sprinkle

limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.

limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Store dry ingredients in a labeled airtight container in a dry place, out of reach of children and pets.

recipes.name: Plastic Container Odor Soak

limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.

recipes.name: Musty Book Deodorizing Box
recipes.prepare: Place the dish of baking soda in the tub.
recipes.apply: Stand the dry book upright in the tub beside (not touching) the baking soda, seal, and leave 48 hours to 1 week. Never sprinkle powder on pages.
limits: Valuable or moldy books: consult a conservator.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.

recipes.name: Sneaker Overnight Deodorizer
recipes.prepare: Spoon baking soda into each filter and close with a rubber band to make a sachet.
recipes.apply: Tuck a sachet into each shoe overnight; remove before wearing. Re-use until the soda clumps.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Store dry ingredients in a labeled airtight container in a dry place, out of reach of children and pets.

recipes.name: Gym Bag Odor Sock
recipes.prepare: Pour baking soda into the sock and knot the top.
recipes.apply: Keep in the gym bag between uses; replace monthly. Air the bag out and wash its lining when possible.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Store dry ingredients in a labeled airtight container in a dry place, out of reach of children and pets.

recipes.name: Car Floor Mat Deodorizer
recipes.prepare: Remove and shake out mats.
recipes.apply: Sprinkle carpeted mats and floor, leave 30 minutes with doors open, then vacuum thoroughly.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Store dry ingredients in a labeled airtight container in a dry place, out of reach of children and pets.

recipes.name: Smoke Odor Wall Wash

recipes.apply: Wash walls from the bottom up with a well-wrung sponge, then rinse with plain water. Ventilate. Repaint with a stain-blocking primer if odor persists.

recipes.name: Musty Basement Odor Bowls
ing: 2 cups baking soda divided between 2 shallow bowls
recipes.prepare: Fix leaks first and run a dehumidifier; odors come from moisture.
recipes.apply: Place bowls in the musty area, stir weekly, and replace monthly. Keep humidity below about 50%.

recipes.name: Garbage Disposal Citrus Peel Freshen
ing: Peel of 1 lemon or lime, cut into 1-inch pieces
recipes.prepare: Run cold water.
recipes.apply: Feed peels a few at a time into the running disposal with cold water and run 15 seconds after the last piece. Use occasionally; too many peels can clog.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.

recipes.name: Laundry Hamper Sprinkle
recipes.prepare: Empty the hamper.
recipes.apply: Sprinkle into the bottom of the hamper or bag; it goes into the wash with clothes as a booster.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.

recipes.name: Diaper Pail Wash and Deodorize
recipes.prepare: Empty the pail and wear gloves.
recipes.apply: Scrub with soapy water, rinse, dry in the sun if possible, and sprinkle baking soda in the bottom before adding a new liner.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh for each use. Pour leftovers down a household drain with running water.

recipes.prepare: Run hot water for 30 seconds.
recipes.apply: Pour baking soda and salt into the drain, follow with hot water, wait 15 minutes, then flush with more hot water.
limits: Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Nothing to store; use immediately.

recipes.name: Greasy Kitchen Drain Soap Flush

recipes.apply: Cutting boards, counters, sinks, toothbrush holders, kids' toys (rinse after).
limits: Not a verified sanitizer: it may reduce some germs, but no public-health agency lists it as a household sanitizing method. For germ-kill, use a bleach recipe marked Sanitize or Disinfect.
Can lighten fabric and colored grout. Never in the same bottle as vinegar.
Keep hydrogen peroxide in its brown bottle and never in the same bottle as vinegar.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Opened bottles lose strength in 1 to 6 months. Pour a little into the sink drain: if it no longer fizzes, replace it.

recipes.name: Ant trail spray
recipes.prepare: Spray ant trails, entry points and the ants, then wipe up. Repeat daily for a week.
recipes.apply: Erases the scent trail ants follow. Pair with the borax ant bait to reach the nest.
limits: Not for stone. Peppermint oil is harmful to cats; skip it in cat homes.
Acidic: keep off marble, granite and other natural stone, and never use with bleach.
Keep pets away while in use.
Pest control: not a cleaner or sanitizer.
recipes.storage: 3 months.

recipes.name: Borax ant bait
ing: Cotton balls and small lidded containers with holes punched in the lid
recipes.prepare: Dissolve the sugar and borax in the water. Soak cotton balls and put them in the small containers. Set them along ant trails. Ants carry the bait to the colony; expect results in 3 to 7 days.
recipes.apply: Sugar ants in kitchens, bathrooms and along baseboards.
limits: Borax is toxic if swallowed. Place baits only where children and pets can't reach.
Harmful if swallowed: label it and store it out of reach of children.
Keep pets away while in use.
Pest control: not a cleaner or sanitizer.
recipes.storage: The liquid keeps 1 month in a labeled jar.

recipes.name: Insecticidal soap for plants
ing: 1 tbsp liquid castile soap (no degreasers or additives)
recipes.prepare: Mix in a spray bottle. Spray aphids, mealybugs, whiteflies and spider mites directly, including leaf undersides, in early morning or evening. Rinse plants with plain water after a few hours. Repeat every 4 to 7 days.
recipes.apply: Houseplants, vegetable gardens, roses.
limits: Test on a few leaves first; it can burn ferns, succulents and plants in hot sun. Don't spray bees or open blooms.
Pest control: not a cleaner or sanitizer.
recipes.storage: Mix fresh weekly.
recipes.replaces: diluted store-bought ready-to-use insect spray (bucket or soak)

recipes.name: Fruit fly trap
ing: A jar, plastic wrap and a toothpick
recipes.prepare: Pour the vinegar into the jar and add the soap (it makes flies sink). Cover with plastic wrap and poke 5 or 6 small holes. Replace every 3 to 4 days.
recipes.apply: Fruit flies and fungus gnats near fruit bowls, drains and trash.
limits: Also remove the source: overripe fruit and damp drains.
Pest control: not a cleaner or sanitizer.
recipes.storage: Replace every few days.

recipes.name: Peppermint spider deterrent
recipes.prepare: Combine in a spray bottle and shake before each use. Spray window frames, door thresholds, corners and vents weekly.
recipes.apply: Deters spiders and some crawling insects. Evidence is limited: it's a deterrent, not a kill spray.
limits: Toxic to cats and harmful to dogs if licked or inhaled heavily. Keep away from fish tanks and birds.
Essential oils are optional; skip them in homes with cats, dogs or birds.
Keep pets away while in use.
Pest control: not a cleaner or sanitizer.
recipes.storage: 1 month.

recipes.name: Diatomaceous earth insect barrier
ing: A squeeze duster or soft brush
recipes.prepare: Put on a dust mask. Puff a thin, barely visible line along baseboards, behind appliances and into cracks. Leave 3 to 7 days, vacuum, and reapply. It only works while dry.
recipes.apply: Ants, silverfish, roaches, fleas in carpet, crawling garden pests.
limits: Food-grade only, never pool-grade. The fine dust irritates lungs. Keep it off pets' faces.
Keep pets away while in use.
Pest control: not a cleaner or sanitizer.
recipes.storage: Dry, sealed container, indefinitely.

recipes.name: Stovetop simmer pot
recipes.prepare: Bring to a boil, then simmer on the lowest heat. Top up the water every 30 minutes. Refrigerate between uses.
recipes.apply: Whole-home scent that covers cooking and pet odors without sprays.
limits: Never leave it unattended; a dry pot can scorch or start a fire.
Cleans only: this recipe is not a sanitizer or disinfectant.
recipes.storage: Reuse for 2 to 3 days from the fridge.
